text:
mia: Heads up — inconsistent rate/quota headers from hosted responses. Some 429s include Retry-After, others only have variants like `x-ratelimit-reset-ms` or `quota-remaining`. Breaking the Python SDK backoff util. Anyone seen this?
omar: saw a repro yesterday from a customer. server varies header names and casing depending on routing. saw `quota-remaining` and `x-rate-limit-reset` in one request.
sam: repro with curl:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset-Ms: 1670000000000
No Retry-After header.
cheng: that explains it — current SDK logic expects `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-Reset` exactly. Fails to parse reset when it's `-ms` or lowercase.
mia: proposal: make header parsing tolerant. accept common variants (case-insensitive), accept seconds and epoch-ms, fallback to computing reset from Date header. expose a small RateLimitInfo on the response with normalized fields: limit, remaining, reset_at.
eva: +1. Also need an async-friendly backoff helper for the aiohttp client. Suggested API snippet: `@dataclass class RateLimitInfo: limit: Optional[int]; remaining: Optional[int]; reset_at: Optional[float]  # epoch seconds` and `def parse_rate_headers(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> RateLimitInfo` and `async def backoff_and_retry_async(fn: Callable[..., Awaitable[Response]], *args, retries: int = 3, backoff_factor: float = 0.5) -> Response` — helper should inspect 429, look for Retry-After, then RateLimitInfo.reset_at, then exponential backoff.
omar: prefer `reset_at` epoch seconds over delta; easier for tests and logs. prefer dataclass over dict for typing.
cheng: typing note: add explicit return types and a `types.pyi` stub so mypy picks up async overloads. maybe overloads for sync vs async clients or generic TypeVar.
ci-bot: created GH issue #4123: "py-sdk: robust rate header parsing + async backoff helper" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4123)
mia: i'll add a short design doc and PR. plan: parse header permutations, add RateLimitInfo to Response.meta, add `parse_rate_headers` util and `backoff_and_retry_async` + sync `backoff_and_retry`. tests: unit tests for permutations and a small integration that fakes 429 with different headers.
sam: i'll write unit tests and an examples/ratelimit/ aiohttp example.
eva: ping @cheng for types review when PR is up.
omar: i'll take the PR, aim for draft tomorrow morning. will include tests for: header casing, `-ms` vs seconds, missing headers with Date fallback, and missing Date.
mia: perfect, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
sam: lgtm
eva: thanks!
cheng: will review typings.
